evidence_items.explanation: In the early-ChatGPT era, about half of answers had errors. Even programmers who were allowed to check with external tools missed the misinformation 39% of the time, partly because the answers were well written. That fits 'good-looking output' hiding errors.

evidence_items.explanation: Independent testers in February 2025 found AI search tools were often wrong, and judged that their confident tone makes errors hard for users to spot.

unresolved_gaps: No study found measures specifically whether 'most people' miss subtle LLM errors. The closest figure (39% missed, by programmers who could use external tools) is below a majority.
Error rates vary widely by task and model, so 'often' depends on the domain.
